It probably makes sense to split curves up in such a way that they are sorted from left to right, or somehow vertically partition so that you can quickly discard all the curves that are fully to the right of the pixel you're looking at.
This specific optimization is likely very font-dependent in terms of how effective it is.
In my early experiments, I actually didn't see any speed up at all, which is why I haven't bothered finalizing it.
It's possible, though, that for some fonts, this type of thing might be even necessary.
And last, another thing I think might be worth exploring is actually some form of curve compression.
Even though I'm storing all the curve data as 16-bit floats, there is still quite a bit of redundancy because a lot of the control points are actually shared between neighboring curves.
I'll probably circle back to this in the future when I add support for CJK languages or other languages that have a lot more glyphs than English.
